extracted.intended_audience: Navy managers, procurement officers, policymakers, and researchers studying OMB Circular A-76/Commercial Activities implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical evaluation of post-award costs and performance effects of contracting out under OMB Circular A-76, focusing on Navy supply operations (food service and storage/warehousing) on the U.S. West Coast and Hawaii; identifies hidden costs, assesses cost-comparison accuracy, performance measurement, and proposes policy/research recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The study identifies "the need for post-award guidance and policy" as an issue in CA program implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of centralized post-award guidance contributes to inconsistent handling of post-award costs and program controls; recommendations include developing specific post-award policy to standardize practices across activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for increased claimant guidance at the field level
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors note "the need for increased claimant guidance at the field level."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-level claimants require clearer instruction to implement and monitor conversions; lack of claimant guidance leads to undercounting or misallocation of costs in post-award periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of an adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The thesis reports "the absence of an adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adequate accounting/system is necessary to capture all relevant post-award costs; without it, 'hidden costs' remain unrecorded and cost comparisons are inaccurate. Strengthening accounting and control mechanisms is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for increased contract administration staffing (understaffing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study lists "the need for increased contract administration staffing" (and conversely, understaffing of contract administration) as a problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate contract administration personnel are required to monitor contractor performance, enforce terms, and track post-award costs; understaffing undermines oversight and allows performance or cost issues to persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out
rubrics_metrics.description: The thesis identifies "a problem with budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting out can restrict local managers' ability to reallocate funds in response to changing needs; evaluating budgetary flexibility post-conversion is essential when assessing net savings or operational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing problems with performance definition
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the issues identified is "continuing problems with performance definition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems arise when performance metrics (surrogates) do not reflect true service quality; ill-defined Performance Requirements Summaries can be manipulated leading to misleading assessments of contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: Commercial Activities vs Governmental Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular's distinction: Commercial Activities are those that can be provided by the private sector; Governmental functions are "so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Government employees."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a function is legitimately commercial (e.g., word processing, ADP support may be embedded and reviewable) or governmental (examples: criminal investigations, management of Military Services, conduct of foreign relations). Misclassification can lead to inappropriate conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Relevant Costs in Cost Comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant costs are defined as "expected future costs (expected future revenues) that will differ among alternatives" and exclude costs incurred regardless of alternative or sunk costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparisons should include only costs that differ between the government and contractor alternatives. Example: utility costs that would be incurred either way are irrelevant. After identifying relevant costs, determine the incremental cost (difference between alternatives) as the decision basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental cost principle
rubrics_metrics.description: "An incremental cost is the difference in total cost between two alternatives."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use incremental cost as the metric for choosing between in-house and contractor performance. Ensure all relevant future-differing costs are included before computing the incremental cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of pre-award cost estimates versus actual post-award costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Central controversy: whether a pre-award bid is an accurate estimate of actual post-award program savings in contracted operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the reliability/accuracy of pre-award estimates by comparing predicted savings to realized post-award expenditures, including any unanticipated or unrecorded costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and measurement of unrecorded ('hidden') costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question: "Are there unrecorded costs associated with contracting out a supply operation?" and "What is the magnitude of these unrecorded costs and what specifically are they?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically search for costs not captured in formal accounting systems (transition costs, oversight, performance shortfalls, loss of flexibility, etc.), categorize them, and estimate magnitudes where possible; these influence the net savings calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of unrecorded costs on activity, supported units, and major claimant
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question: "What is the impact of these 'hidden' costs on the activity, the units it supports, and the activity's major claimant?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate downstream operational effects (e.g., service degradation, increased workload elsewhere, readiness impacts) and assess how hidden costs alter benefits to supported units or claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization: Which unrecorded costs are most significant
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question: "Which unrecorded costs are most significant?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank unrecorded costs by financial magnitude and operational significance to focus mitigation and policy responses on the highest-impact areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation: Ways to minimize hidden costs via acquisition controls, specification, and QA
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question: "Are there ways to minimize these costs through acquisition control techniques, improved specification writing and/or quality control measures?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine procurement strategies, contract specifications, and quality assurance mechanisms to reduce post-award surprises; robust PRS, tighter specs, and strengthened oversight are potential solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of post-award performance effectiveness (contracted vs in-house)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question: "Is there a significant difference in the post-award performance effectiveness of supply operations that have been contracted out and those which haven't? If there are performance differences, what are those differences and what are their basic causes?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and compare objective and surrogate performance indicators (timeliness, quality, readiness impacts) for contracted and in-house operations; analyze root causes for any observed performance differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of efficiency measures in non-profit (government) organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The thesis questions the use of efficiency measures in non-profit organizations because outputs/benefits are difficult to measure compared to profit firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating government functions, recognize limits of single-metric efficiency measures; consider multi-dimensional performance and qualitative benefits that efficiency-focused metrics may miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and vulnerability of performance proxies (measurement manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance cannot be measured directly, so "proxies" are used; proxies may not reflect actual quality and can be manipulated (apple color vs taste example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design performance metrics that map closely to the desired service quality; beware incentives that encourage gaming of surrogate measures; monitor for unintended manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of costs and budgetary implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter/section focus: "Accuracy of Costs and Budgetary Implications."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how cost-accounting practices affect budget reporting and flexibility; inaccuracies may distort perceived savings and affect resource allocation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training adequacy and CA training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The thesis examines "Training Issues" and lists "CA Training Requirements."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether personnel involved in cost comparisons, contracting, and post-award administration have adequate training; insufficient training can lead to misestimation of costs and weak oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type and method of procurement as an outcome factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations list "Contract Type and Method of Procurement" as a factor influencing outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different contract forms and procurement methods change risk allocation, cost predictability, and contractor performance; evaluate which types produce better post-award cost and performance outcomes for the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of mobilization on contractor operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation notes "Impact of Mobilization on Contractor Operations" as an issue to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contractor ability to support mobilization or surge requirements; risks in contingency readiness can represent hidden costs or lowered effectiveness of contracted functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sample-based research methods (questionnaire/interview) for post-award evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological criteria: sample selection, questionnaire results, and informal interviews are used to gather post-award data (14 West Coast activities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating post-award outcomes, combine archival data with questionnaires and interviews of claimants, major/sub-claimants, and administrators to identify issues not reflected in accounting records; document sample selection and limitations.
